title: Design and Development of an Integrated Secure Data Erasure and Advanced File Recovery Tool for Digital Forensics and Data Sanitization
description:
• Background With the rapid growth of digital storage technologies, organizations, government agencies, law enforcement units, enterprises, and individual users face two major challenges: securely destroying sensitive data to prevent unauthorized recovery and recovering deleted digital evidence during forensic investigations. Existing solutions generally focus on either secure data deletion or file recovery and often support limited storage technologies and file systems. This forces investigators and cybersecurity professionals to use multiple tools, increasing complexity, cost, and operational inefficiencies. Therefore, there is a need for a unified platform that integrates secure data sanitization with advanced forensic-grade file recovery and carving capabilities.
• Description The proposed solution aims to develop an integrated software platform consisting of three core modules: (1) Secure Drive Eraser, (2) Secure File & (3) Folder Eraser, and Advanced File Carving and Recovery. The Secure Drive Eraser Module should securely sanitize HDDs, SSDs, USB drives, memory cards, and external storage devices while providing verification mechanisms, audit logging, tamper-resistant reporting, and compliance with industry and government data destruction standards. The Secure File and Folder Eraser Module should enable selective secure deletion of files and folders, remove associated metadata and residual traces, support batch operations, verify erasure success, and provide audit reporting across multiple file systems and operating systems. The Advanced File Carving and Recovery Module should recover deleted files from formatted, damaged, or corrupted media using signature-based, structure-based, and intelligent carving techniques. It should support recovery without file system metadata, fragmented file reconstruction, automatic classification of recovered files, confidence scoring, and comprehensive forensic reporting while preserving evidential integrity.
• Expected Solution The expected outcome is an integrated software platform that combines secure data sanitization and forensic recovery capabilities within a single environment. The solution should provide (1) secure drive erasure with verification and reporting, (2) secure file and folder deletion with metadata cleansing, (3) advanced file carving and recovery from formatted media, support for multiple storage devices and file systems, automated classification and validation of recovered files, comprehensive audit logs and forensic reports, a user-friendly graphical interface, and compliance with forensic and data sanitization standards. Expected deliverables include an integrated software tool, (1) Secure Drive Eraser Module, (2) Secure File and Folder Eraser Module, (3) Advanced File Carving and Recovery Module, Reporting and Audit Management System, User Interface Dashboard, validation and testing documentation, user manuals, technical documentation, and performance evaluation reports. The solution should improve secure data disposal practices, reduce the risk of unauthorized data recovery, enhance forensic investigation capabilities, increase recovery rates from damaged storage media, reduce investigation time, improve compliance and auditability, and provide a unified platform for secure sanitization and forensic recovery operations.
summary: Innovation (1/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a blockchain & cybersecurity problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Blockchain & Cybersecurity. Tech Depth (2/5): centers on compliance. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 13/30 -> Red verdict.

detail.title: Design and Development of an Integrated Secure Data Erasure and Advanced File Recovery Tool for Digital Forensics and Data Sanitization

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a single tool that combines secure data wiping, with verification and audit logs, and forensic-grade file recovery, replacing the current need for investigators to juggle multiple separate tools for these two related jobs.
overview.why_it_matters: Organizations and forensic investigators currently need multiple disconnected tools for secure erasure and file recovery, adding cost and complexity. One unified, verified platform genuinely simplifies real forensic workflows.
pain_points: Existing solutions focus on either secure deletion or file recovery, rarely both together.
Limited storage technology and file system support forces use of multiple tools.
No unified platform integrates sanitization with forensic-grade recovery and carving.
overview.background: Organizations, law enforcement, and forensic investigators need both secure data destruction and forensic file recovery capability, but existing tools are fragmented across separate, single-purpose solutions.
overview.whats_being_asked: An integrated platform with three modules: Secure Drive Eraser, Secure File/Folder Eraser, and Advanced File Carving/Recovery, supporting multiple storage technologies and file systems, with verification and audit logging.
expected_solution: Secure drive erasure (HDDs, SSDs, USB, memory cards) with verification.
Advanced file carving and recovery across multiple file systems.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Low as scored. Both secure erasure and file recovery/carving are established, well-documented technical domains individually, the innovation is in genuine, working integration across many storage/filesystem types.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Low as scored, but this understates real breadth, supporting multiple storage technologies (HDD, SSD, USB, memory cards) and multiple file systems for both erasure and recovery is genuinely broad engineering scope.

competitive_landscape.note: Niche digital-forensics tooling PS, requires genuine understanding of both secure-erasure standards and file-system-level recovery techniques.

innovation.note: Both component technologies are well-established, real value is in genuine integration breadth, not novel technique.

invention.note: Achievable using established secure-erasure standards (NIST 800-88) and open-source file-carving techniques, real effort in breadth of storage/filesystem coverage.

technical_feasibility.note: Full coverage across all named storage types and file systems isn't achievable in 36 hours, scope to 1-2 storage types and file systems demonstrated genuinely well.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine operational value for forensic investigators, a narrow, specialized professional audience.

architecture.note: Two distinct capability modules (erasure, recovery) with a shared audit/verification layer, manageable if scoped honestly.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Red, mainly due to low innovation and the real breadth challenge (supporting many storage types and file systems is far broader than 36 hours allows). Scope to one storage type (e.g. a standard file system on an HDD/SSD) and demonstrate both erasure and recovery genuinely and verifiably for it.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Established secure-erasure standards (NIST 800-88 and similar) and open-source file-carving techniques provide credible technical grounding to build on.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Attempting broad coverage across all named storage types and file systems will result in shallow, unconvincing coverage everywhere, scope aggressively to one combination done well.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Scope explicitly to one storage type and one file system (e.g. a standard drive with a common file system) and build genuine, verified erasure and recovery for it, rather than claiming broad multi-technology coverage.

idea_0_4: Choose one storage type and file system combination to build fully.
Research established secure-erasure standards (NIST 800-88 patterns) and file-carving/recovery techniques.
Split: one person on secure erasure with verification, one on file carving/recovery.
prototype_4_22: Build secure erasure with a real verification mechanism (confirming data is genuinely unrecoverable).
Build file carving/recovery for your chosen file system.
Start audit logging for both modules.
integration_22_30: Connect erasure, recovery, and audit logging into one coherent platform.
Test erasure verification genuinely, confirm erased data is actually unrecoverable using your own recovery module.
Test recovery against genuinely deleted (not corrupted) test files to confirm real carving capability.
polish_30_36: Polish the platform for genuine forensic-investigator usability.
Rehearse a live demo: erase a test file with verification, then attempt recovery of a different deleted file, showing both capabilities genuinely working.
Prepare to be honest about your single-storage-type scope versus the full multi-technology vision.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Demonstrate the erasure verification genuinely, erase a file, then attempt to recover it with your own recovery module and show it fails, that cross-validation between your two modules is concrete, credible proof rather than claimed capability.

strengths: Established technical standards and techniques provide credible grounding.
Genuine operational value for forensic investigators if scoped honestly.
weaknesses: Full breadth across all named storage types and file systems isn't achievable in 36 hours.
Low innovation ceiling, differentiation depends on genuine verification rigor, not feature breadth.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced, with real research into established erasure standards.
team_fit.approach: Choose one storage/filesystem combination and build it genuinely and verifiably, rather than attempting broad shallow coverage.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard file I/O and basic carving-pattern-matching scaffolding.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly implementing genuine secure-erasure verification and real file-carving techniques, that requires real filesystem and storage forensics domain knowledge.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded erasure tool without genuine verification could give false assurance that data is unrecoverable when it isn't, a serious issue for a security-sanitization tool.

data_resource_availability.status: No real sensitive data should be used for testing, use your own constructed test files.

judge_qna.question: How do you actually verify erasure was successful, not just claim it?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Demonstrate your verification mechanism directly, ideally by attempting recovery with your own tool and showing it fails on erased data.
judge_qna.follow_up: What erasure standard (e.g. NIST 800-88 clear/purge) does your approach align with, and why?

judge_qna.question: Why did you scope to one storage type/file system instead of the full range named in the PS?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be direct that full breadth isn't achievable in 36 hours, and your chosen combination demonstrates the core capability that would extend to others with additional engineering time.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would change technically when adding support for a second storage type?
